limits.statement: The profiles python-flask, php-laravel and node-fastify pin no framework version: versionPin.framework is null in their modules. The record states their framework version as UNKNOWN (value null) and does not fill it in from any other file. For the other four profiles the record repeats the version the profile declares and marks it DECLARED; it is not checked against a lock file or an installed framework, and the declaration of csharp-aspnet-core, net8.0 sample, names a sample target, not a package version. adapters/http-wave-a/python-flask/SCOPE.json states a Flask version for its own oracle; that pin belongs to the scope record and is not copied into the profile row.

The profiles go-gin, php-laravel and python-flask carry the marker historical-pass-needs-leaf-rerun. It is a string in each module that names an earlier pass of the upstream layer and asks for a re-run on the leaf; it is not a pass of the leaf. This record re-ran the three leaves at the base commit on inputs that came out of the in-repo analyzers (the fixtures marked upstream-real; the Flask one runs the python-scope static runner over the eight in-repo Flask fixture directories) and keeps their outputs. That is not a comparison against a real third-party repository: no such comparison, repository, commit or artifact is recorded for these leaves, and the marker text is history, never read as a pass.

realRepoComparison is one plain string in each of the seven profile objects (the ASP.NET module repeats it in the evidence of its outputs). The strings name no repository, commit, command, exit code or artifact hash, and no code in the layer checks them. The profile rows of this record repeat each string and add a marker kind, which is this record's reading of the string, not a property of the code.
The csharp-aspnet-core profile and the evidence of its two upstream-real fixture outputs carry realRepoComparison BLOCKED_INFRA. This record does not unblock that comparison and records none for C#.

The python-django profile has state blocked-upstream-fact-gap and its leaf builds no route: in every replayed case the output has status blocked and no route. With no T06 shadow, or one that is not shaped like one, the only unknown is DJANGO_DRF_UPSTREAM_FACTS_MISSING and the two outputs are equal. With a T06 shadow the leaf keeps the url registrations as observations whose methodSemantics is not-declared-by-urlconf and adds DRF_ACTION_METHOD_FACT_MISSING and the T06 unknowns, still without a route. The python-scope run shows status blocked and no route in all seven Django fixture directories. Implementing this leaf (T12-03) is not part of this record.

The node-fastify profile has state blocked-upstream-fact-gap and its leaf ignores its input: with or without T04 facts it returns status blocked, no route and the single unknown FASTIFY_UPSTREAM_RECEIVER_FACT_MISSING, and the two outputs are equal. Implementing this leaf (T12-03) is not part of this record.

The NestJS leaf only projects bskel.internal.js-ts-structure/0 facts (with js-ts-source-facts/0), and the scope record of the layer states that no producer of those structure facts exists in the repository. The only file outside this layer that names the contract at the base commit is the scope verifier of the HTTP legacy layer (T11). The NestJS fixtures are therefore hand-fed: no path from NestJS source code to a route is replayed, the projector against the framework oracle is blocked, and the marker PASS_STATIC_REAL_REPO in the profile is a claim of the code that this record does not reproduce.

The NestJS leaf gives neither a route nor an unknown for a method whose name is computed even when it carries a route decorator, for a class whose Controller decorator is not bound to the import from @nestjs/common, and for a member that is not a method. The fixture with the first two cases produces no route, no unknown and no observation. An output without routes therefore cannot tell a controller without routes from one whose members were skipped. Only decorators that are present but not called, and controller or method paths that are not string literals, become unknowns.

Some route registrations leave no trace in the outputs. The T08 analyzer gives neither route nor fact for app.Map without a verb and for a Go Handle call with the method TRACE (the C# source that also holds app.Map yields one route and no unknown; the Go source that also holds the TRACE call yields two routes and three unknowns, none of them the TRACE call); a C# MapGet path without a leading slash arrives as an absolute path; the Flask dynamic route factory and imperative registration directories give no route and no flag at the T06 shadow and at the leaf; and the T06 registration-limitation flags of the generated routes, router prefix and normal Flask directories do not reach the leaf output. The outputs of the leaves are therefore a lower bound of the routes of the scanned source, not a list.

The Flask leaf does not read registration.limitations of the T06 shadow: a registration that carries the T06 limitation about register_blueprint(url_prefix=...) mount overrides gives the same output as one without it (the two fixtures are equal), although the profile lists register_blueprint mount-prefix override composition among its unknown conditions. A route that T06 flags as possibly mounted elsewhere is a plain route in the leaf output.

The ASP.NET Core leaf builds routes with makeRoute and never calls routeOrUnknown, so a hand-fed route fact whose method is ANY or whose path is not absolute makes it throw a TypeError instead of producing an unknown, while the Gin, Laravel and Flask leaves build their routes through routeOrUnknown and keep such facts as unknowns. The real C# analyzer emits neither case (a relative path arrives as an absolute one), so only hand-fed input reaches the throw.

projection refuses an operationId on a route (TypeError) and nowhere else: an observation that carries an operationId passes through unchanged. The guard is the only mechanism that keeps a leaf from synthesizing operation ids, and routes have no identity field of their own; no replayed route carries an operationId.

projection sorts and wraps the routes it is given and does not call makeRoute: a route with method ANY and a relative path passes through, also under a blocked profile. The guarantees on routes (explicit method, absolute path, provenance) and the empty routes of a blocked leaf hold because each leaf builds its routes with makeRoute or routeOrUnknown, not because projection enforces them; the baseline test re-checks them on the replayed outputs of the leaves.

defineProfile forces registration unregistered, productionDefault false and runtimeTested false but keeps a t19Review value that the caller passes (the fixture passes APPROVED and gets it back), and it freezes only the top level of the profile it returns. The seven profiles show NOT_REVIEWED because none of them passes the field; nothing in the helper enforces it.

Nothing connects the leaf contract to contracts/next or to the capability vocabulary of scanners/capability-next: no script of the layer imports or names contracts/next, sdk/next, scanners/capability-next or schemas/next, and the leaf status (candidate or blocked) is not one of the five capability states (supported, partial, unsupported, unknown, not-applicable). A leaf output is not a capability record and no conversion exists. The bridge is a promotion gate named in INTERFACE_RFC.md and is not built here.

No file outside adapters/http-wave-a and test/http-wave-a names the leaf contract bskel.internal.http-wave-a-leaf/0 at the base commit. Nothing outside the layer reads the shape of a leaf output, so that shape is pinned only by the tests of the layer; a consumer would have to bring its own conformance test (a promotion gate in INTERFACE_RFC.md).

No leaf is a supported adapter. Every profile is defined through defineProfile, which forces registration unregistered, productionDefault false and runtimeTested false; the leaf outputs say unregistered and productionDefault false and have status candidate or blocked; no replayed output carries a key named supported, support, capability or capabilities. The record changes none of it: an unknown, unsupported or blocked case is never marked supported, and a candidate is not a promise.

The Flask and Django fixtures of the python-scope run need python3 and rg. The record states the versions of the machine it was generated on (python3 and rg in environment.external_programs). The python-scope static runner output was identical on python 3.11.15, 3.12.13 and 3.14.8 when this record was made; other interpreters and other ripgrep versions were not run, and no test compares the live versions with the record.

The python-scope verifier lists directory and file names under adapters/ and scanners/ (rule adapter-appeared) to see whether a scanner or adapter for a scope-only framework has appeared, and the module registry lists scanners/adapters/ and loads every file in it. The extracted copy of the baseline holds only the pinned files, so those listings are not the listings of the full repository; the record pins the git tree ids of adapters, scanners and scanners/adapters at the base commit, which only the pinned commit can answer. A file added to these directories later is invisible to the pinned-file checks.

Neither the prose of INTERFACE_RFC.md nor the descriptive values of interface-rfc.vocabulary.json nor the descriptive keywords of leaf-contract.schema.json are compared with the code, so the edits listed here are not reported by interface-rfc.test.mjs; its edit matrices found them and its last test binds this text to their lists. In the RFC text: the title text, the headings (replaced or removed), the prose sentences (a word replaced, a sentence appended, a line removed unless that line carries a word the test requires), the claims of the Status line, and a backticked word in the Status line swapped for another word of the vocabulary. In the vocabulary, when the RFC text is changed to match: the input text of a leaf, the blocker and closes_when text of a gate, the limits named by a gate, the text of a schema gap, the ownership wording for T12, the text of a key rule, the lists of foreign schemas and foreign keys (an element added, removed or replaced), and the unusable-input wording of a shared function. In the schema: the schema title, the schema description, the schema $id, a schema $comment and the minLength of profileId. These lists are not proved complete: an edit that no matrix tries, for example a backticked word swapped on a prose line other than the Status line, is untested, and the comparison of the RFC with the code is not proved complete.

verification.recomputed: bytes, git_blob_sha1 and sha256 of every pinned file, per-file and total test counts, the exit code and counts of both commands, the first runner line, every profile row against the live export of its leaf module, every fixture output hash and every expected value, the invariants of every replayed leaf output, the match counts, reference lists and git tree ids that the limits carry, the status and channels of every limit against the table in baseline-record.test.mjs, and the installed version of every package in environment.loaded_packages against package-lock.json at the base commit.
levels: always: the record is well formed, and any single tampered hash, size, test count, exit code, expected value, limit status or commit id is reported; artifact_digest covers every field except its own value, so an edit of a limit statement, a fixture class, a call, a title or this text that is not re-sealed is reported

live files: size, sha256 and blob id are recomputed from the checkout; a file that disagrees in one hash or in size alone is damage and fails; a file that matches neither hash is drift, which skips the live replays while the pinned commit decides

pinned commit: the base commit is fetched once when absent and the sizes and digests of all pinned files, the runner included, are recomputed from its own blobs; if the commit is unavailable the test fails, and only BASELINE_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 turns that into an explicit skip
ancestry: a shallow checkout is deepened with git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin and the base commit must be an ancestor of HEAD

commands: both recorded commands are re-run in an extracted copy of the base commit (node_modules linked from the checkout once the installed versions equal environment.loaded_packages, which package-lock.json at the base commit states) and must reproduce exit code, counts, per-file counts and every fixture output

profiles and fixtures: each profile row equals what the live module exports, every leaf module has a row, and every fixture is replayed twice on the live files with its output hash and expected values compared
limits: the match counts of the text evidence are recomputed from the pinned files, the reference lists with git grep at the pinned commit and the tree ids with git rev-parse at the pinned commit
not_recomputed: ci_observations: read once from the CI API (gh api, read-only) and kept for traceability; no test re-reads them
environment: describes the machine this record was generated on; the python3 and rg versions are not compared with the machine that runs the test

prose: limit statements, fixture origins, the title, observed_on and this text are bound only by artifact_digest, which reports an edit that is not re-sealed; an editor who re-seals the record is caught only by review of the diff and by the recomputed values above; the statement of the limit interface-rfc-prose-is-not-compared is also checked by interface-rfc.test.mjs for the phrases that name each group of edits that survive its matrices
the files inside the installed packages (ajv, ajv-formats and the packages they require): not hashed; only their versions are compared with package-lock.json at the base commit

the import scan that decides which packages must be installed is textual: lines that start with // , /* or * and scripts below a fixtures directory are skipped, and a specifier built at run time is not seen

hand-fed inputs: the literals of the hand-fed fixtures were written by the author of this record; only the outputs of the code at the base commit are recomputed, not the faithfulness of the literals to any real producer
files added by this item: this record, the baseline test and its library, the interface document and its test, vocabulary and schema are created after the base commit and are not pinned in files
